title: This Worm Has No Mouth and No Stomach, and Grows Over 6 Feet
subject: giant tube worm

scenes.text: This worm has no mouth, no stomach, and it grows taller than you.
It lives miles under the ocean, around vents that blast out hot, toxic water.
There's no sunlight there. So how does it eat?
It carries bacteria inside its body. The bacteria turn the toxic hydrogen sulfide into food.
Its red plume is full of blood, which grabs the sulfide and carries it to the bacteria.
They can grow almost three feet in a year and a half. It isn't eating the vent. It's farming bacteria.

description:
Giant tube worms have no mouth and no stomach, and they grow over six feet tall.
At deep-sea vents, bacteria inside them turn toxic hydrogen sulfide into food, and the worm's blood-red plume carries the sulfide to them. They can grow almost three feet in a year and a half.
What's the strangest animal you know?
first_comment: They were first found at the Galapagos vents in 1977, and scientists were stunned that anything lived there. What would you want to explore on the deep seafloor?
